title: What Is An “NPC” and Where Did the Term Come From?
titleZh: 从游戏走到现实，NPC这个词经历了什么
summary:
如果你上网时间够久——或者身边有青少年，或是认识对网络流行语特别熟悉的人——那你很可能听人说过“NPC”这个词。如今，这一缩写已经成为最常见的网络贬损用语之一，但它到底指什么？一般来说，称某人为“NPC”，意味着你认为对方缺乏独立思考能力；说得更直白些，就是对方的意见于你而言无足轻重——不过，这种用法其实并非NPC一词最初的含义。

来源：MentalFloss；作者：Eden Gordon；原文发布时间：2026-04-28 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: If you’ve been on the internet for long enough—or perhaps if there’s a teenager or a particularly slang-savvy adult in your life—you may have heard someone use the term “NPC.” This acronym has become one of the most commonly used slang insults around, but what does it mean? In general, calling someone an “NPC” is a way to tell a person that they lack original thinking skills, or more simply, that their opinion doesn't matter to you—but the term didn't start out that way.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如果你上网时间够久——或者身边有青少年，或是认识对网络流行语特别熟悉的人——那你很可能听人说过“NPC”这个词。如今，这一缩写已经成为最常见的网络贬损用语之一，但它到底指什么？一般来说，称某人为“NPC”，意味着你认为对方缺乏独立思考能力；说得更直白些，就是对方的意见于你而言无足轻重——不过，这种用法其实并非NPC一词最初的含义。

paragraphs.contentEn: “NPC” is an acronym that stands for “non-player character.” It has its roots in the game Dungeons & Dragons, which debuted in 1974. This game allowed players to inhabit various personas and embark on elaborate quests, and often involved giant casts of characters. The original Dungeons & Dragons handbook contained a section that described “non-player characters” and featured some rules about engaging with them. According to the handbook, one could enlist the help of a non-player character, provided these characters were paid regularly, treated fairly, not exposed to excessive dangers, and given bonuses when embarking on risky missions.
paragraphs.contentZh: “NPC”是“non-player character”（非玩家角色）的英文缩写。这个说法最早可追溯至1974年推出的游戏《龙与地下城》。在这款游戏中，玩家可以扮演不同角色，参与剧情复杂的冒险任务，游戏过程中往往有庞大的角色阵容。在《龙与地下城》的初代游戏手册中，设有专门章节对“非玩家角色”作出说明，并列出了与其互动的基本规则。按照手册设定，玩家可以招募非玩家角色来协助自己，但前提是需要定期支付报酬、给予公平对待、避免使其陷入极度危险的境地，并在执行高危任务时支付额外酬劳。

paragraphs.contentEn: As role-playing video games grew in popularity across the following decades, so did non-player characters—who soon were widely referred to as “NPCs.” In the context of video games, the acronym refers to characters that appear onscreen and are not controlled by players—think shop-owners, villains, guides who offer key information along the way, or those random background characters who just float by and add scope to the world of the game.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在随后的几十年里，随着角色扮演类电子游戏日渐流行，非玩家角色也变得越来越常见——很快便被广泛简称为“NPC”。在电子游戏语境中，这一缩写指的是那些出现在游戏画面中、但不由玩家操控的角色——例如商店老板、反派人物、沿途提供关键信息的向导，或是那些随机出现、仅用于丰富游戏世界的背景角色。

paragraphs.contentEn: The term “NPC” began to be used to describe real people as early as the 2010s, when it appeared in some literature created by key members of the LessWrong community, a California-based subculture that subscribes to a philosophical worldview that focuses on eradicating biases and viewing everything with extreme rationality. In this context, “NPCs” referred to people who were perceived to be somehow ineffective or unintelligent. Even at that time, the term was controversial, with writer Maciej Cegłowski arguing that its dehumanizing implications represented “a horrible way to look at the world” in a 2016 essay.
paragraphs.contentZh: 将“NPC”用于形容现实中的人，最早可追溯至2010年代，当时，这一用法出现在美国加州亚文化社群LessWrong部分核心成员的文章中，LessWrong社群奉行一种强调消除偏见、主张以高度理性看待世界的哲学理念。在此语境下，“NPC”被用来指代那些被认为思考效率低下或缺乏思考能力的人。即便在当时，这样的用法也已引起不少争议。2016年，作家马切伊·切格沃夫斯基在一篇文章中批评称，这种带有去人化色彩的词汇暗示，反映出的是一种“极其可怕的世界观”。

paragraphs.contentEn: According to Know Your Meme, “NPC” began to become more popular online thanks to a post that appeared on the forum 4chan in 2016. “I have a theory that there are only a fixed quantity of souls on planet Earth that cycle continuously through reincarnation,” the poster wrote. “However, since the human growth rate is so severe, the soulless extra walking flesh piles around us are NPC’s [sic]...who autonomously follow group think and social trends in order to appear convingly [sic] human.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 据Know Your Meme网站梳理，“NPC”一词在网络上的流行，源于2016年4chan论坛上的一则帖子。发帖者写道：“我有一个猜想：地球上的灵魂数量是固定的，并在不断轮回。但由于人口增长过于剧烈，我们周围那些多出来的、没有灵魂的行尸走肉，其实就是NPC……他们为了看起来更像人类，会自动迎合群体思维和社会潮流。”

paragraphs.contentEn: That same year, a meme called "NPC Wojak"—which featured a sketch of an expressionless, grey-colored man—was first posted on 4chan. Its popularity, as well as the aforementioned post, helped “NPC” to become a popular slang term by 2018. By that time, 4chan users were using the term frequently to refer to people whom they found lacking in critical thinking skills, originality, or opinions.
paragraphs.contentZh: 同年，一张名为“NPC Wojak”的迷因图首次出现在4chan论坛——画中是面无表情的灰白色人物素描。这个形象的走红，连同之前提到的帖子，共同推动了“NPC”在2018年成为一个流行的网络俚语。此时，4chan用户已开始频繁用这个词来指代那些在他们看来缺乏批判性思维、缺少原创观点或没有明确立场的人。

paragraphs.contentEn: In these earlier online iterations, “NPC” was frequently used in political contexts to shut down people with opposing views. Per Know Your Meme, “'NPC' turned into an insult to be used against people who stuck with the mainstream, often by those who held fringe socio-political views. Therefore being called an NPC is akin to being called a person without individuality, originality or personality, who serves only as a background character in other people’s lives.” Critics of the term have questioned the term's fundamentally dehumanizing nature, citing the dangers inherent in implying that those with different views fundamentally lack personhood. Those who use the term would likely gleefully call those critics “NPCs.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 在这一早期的网络讨论中，“NPC”经常被用于政治语境，用以压制不同观点的表达。根据Know Your Meme网站的说法：“‘NPC’逐渐演变为一种贬损性称呼，常被持有边缘社会政治立场的人用来指代那些认同主流观点的人。因此，被称为NPC，某种程度上就等同于被视为缺乏独特性、原创性或完整人格，只是在他人生活中充当背景板的角色。”批评人士对这一词汇本质上带有的去人化色彩提出了质疑，并指出，如果据此暗示意见不同者在本质上不具备完整的人格，这种逻辑本身就存在危险。而使用这一词汇的人，很可能会幸灾乐祸地称这些批评者为“NPC”。

paragraphs.contentEn: Today, “NPC” has become a catch-all term that is generally used to call someone irrelevant, unintelligent, or unoriginal. However, if you find yourself on the receiving end of this term, you might remind whoever’s using it that in video games and Dungeons & Dragons, NPCs are often critical to the plot. They often present quests, deliver important information, and add scope and texture to the game—and, according to the Dungeons & Dragons handbook, they must be compensated regularly and fairly for their labor.
paragraphs.contentZh: 时至今日，“NPC”已成为一种泛化的说法，常被用来贬低某人无足轻重、缺乏思考能力或没有自己的观点。不过，如果你发现自己被贴上了这一标签，或许可以提醒对方：在电子游戏和《龙与地下城》的设定中，NPC往往是推动剧情发展的关键。它们负责发布任务、提供重要情报，也为游戏世界增添层次与细节——而且，根据《龙与地下城》手册的设定，NPC需要为自己的劳动获得定期且公平的报酬。
